summary: Most visitors — including EU, UK, US, Chinese and Indian passport holders — need Azerbaijan's ASAN e-Visa, issued online in about three working days for a 30-day stay. CIS neighbors and Turkey enter visa-free, Gulf nationals can obtain a visa on arrival, and citizens of Armenia are barred from entry.

payments.text: Cards are widely accepted in Baku's shops, restaurants and hotels, but carry manat for regional towns, bazaars, taxis and rural areas.

safety.text: Baku is safe with low street crime. Keep well away from the border with Armenia and do not enter the Karabakh region or other restricted zones without government authorization — landmines and closed military areas remain.

bestTimeToVisit.text: April–June and September–October are comfortable in Baku and the regions; midsummer is hot in the lowlands but pleasant in the Caucasus mountains.

tips.text: Travelers with Armenian citizenship are refused entry, and those of Armenian descent or with evidence of visits to Nagorno-Karabakh face refusal or intense questioning — if this could affect you, contact an Azerbaijani embassy before booking.

Azerbaijan's land borders have been closed to passenger crossings since 2020 and the closure has been extended repeatedly — most travelers can only enter and leave by air, so check the current position before planning an overland route.
If you stay more than 15 days you must be registered with the State Migration Service — hotels usually do it automatically, but private hosts often don't, and fines apply on departure.
Apply only at evisa.gov.az — third-party visa websites charge large markups for the same USD 25 e-Visa.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Azerbaijan?
faq.answer: Most travelers do — but it's easy. Citizens of around 95 countries, including the EU, UK, US, China and India, apply online for the ASAN e-Visa (USD 25, about three working days, 30-day stay). CIS countries, Georgia and Turkey are visa-free, Gulf nationals get a visa on arrival, and the remaining nationalities apply at an embassy.

faq.question: How fast is the ASAN e-Visa?
faq.answer: Standard processing takes about three working days. An urgent service issues the e-Visa within roughly three hours for a higher fee. The visa is valid for 90 days from issue for a single 30-day stay.

faq.question: Can I enter Azerbaijan if I have been to Armenia?
faq.answer: An ordinary visit to Armenia, shown by stamps or an Armenian visa, is generally tolerated, though you should expect extra questions at the border. Evidence of a visit to Nagorno-Karabakh is different — it leads to refusal of entry and a ban. Armenian citizens cannot enter at all.

faq.question: Can I cross into Azerbaijan by land?
faq.answer: Generally no — the land borders (Georgia, Russia, Iran) have been closed to passenger traffic since 2020, with the closure repeatedly extended. Practically all foreign visitors arrive by air. Check whether the policy has changed before planning an overland trip.

faq.question: Do I need to register my stay in Azerbaijan?
faq.answer: Yes, if you stay more than 15 days — registration with the State Migration Service is mandatory. Hotels handle it automatically for their guests; independent travelers staying in apartments must arrange it themselves or face a fine when leaving.
